subject: Sparrow trial: post-call recap & capacity ask
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@getsparrow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Sparrow trial: post-call recap & capacity ask

Hi Aisha — great conversation earlier. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff.

Call summary (30 min)
- Goal: run a 2-week evaluation that validates latency and cost for your real-time summarization pipeline (document -> chunking -> embed -> rerank -> generation).
- Primary success criteria (Sparrow): end-to-end 95th percentile latency < 220ms for 1k token end-to-end request, summary quality >= baseline model (we'll use your labeled eval set) and stable token cost under the agreed budget.
- Secondary: embedding similarity stability, KV cache hit rate >= 60% for repeated docs.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline
- Pre-kickoff (this week): exchange data slices + evaluation prompts (you said ~500 representative docs).
- Day 0 kickoff: confirm test harness, access, and SLA for logging.
- Week 1: functional checks, warm cache, run synthetic load for baseline throughput measurement.
- Week 2: run production-like traffic window (hours-long sessions) and collect metrics + eval set scoring.
- Final readout: 3 business days after trial end — joint report with latency/cost/quality and recommended configs.

Capacity ask (what we recommend based on your traffic profile)
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100-80GB equiv for the duration of the trial to provide predictable tail-latency for cold-starts and KV-resident workloads.
- Autoscale/ burst: policy to allow burst to 8 GPUs (same family) for short windows (up to ~5 minutes sustained) to cover ingestion peaks and heavy rerank workloads.
- Warmup: prewarm embeddings worker and keep KV cache alive for the expected demo traffic windows.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Neha (sales, logistics) + Marissa (solutions engineering, POC runbook, provisioning) + Dev (runtime/devops support).
- Sparrow: Aisha (product lead) + Liam (CTO) as technical approver.

Notes / asks from your side
1) Can you share the 500-doc sample + labeled eval set by EOD Friday? (sparrow_poc_requirements.xlsx referenced).
2) Any org firewall egress restrictions or IP allowlists we should pre-provision?
3) Budget guardrails — confirm if you want Redwood to enforce a hard cap or just alerting during the trial.

I've attached a short template POC runbook (redwood_trial_runbook.pdf) and a one-tab requirements sheet for your team to fill out.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- You: share sample data + confirm allowlist contacts.
- We: provision reserved baseline capacity and share a provisioning window (target: next Wed for kickoff).
- Schedule 45-min kickoff — Neha to propose slots.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Sparrow trial: post-call recap & capacity ask

Thanks Neha — very helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the latency target you listed looks in line with our expectations for summary requests. For throughput, our initial baseline is ~30 concurrent active users with occasional spikes to ~120 concurrent (these manifest as short 60–90s bursts). If you can size for sustained baseline ~2 GPUs and burst to 8 for the short windows, that maps to our real traffic shape.
- Data: we'll upload the 500-doc slice and the labeled eval set to the shared drive by Thursday EOD.
- Security/compliance: please send the SOC2 questionnaire link — our procurement will need that before signing the trial terms. Liam flagged data retention/ingress IPs; our infra is behind an allowlist and we can provide firewall rules.

Two asks before kickoff:
1) Can you provide an estimated per-hour cost for the baseline vs burst capacity so I can pre-clear with procurement?
2) Who owns the autoscale policy & cooldowns during trial — Redwood or Sparrow? We prefer Redwood to operate autoscale with a policy we approve.

Happy to take a 20-minute sync if helpful.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Head of Product, Sparrow Systems
aisha@getsparrow.ai

Quick technical plan and costing sketch for Neha/Aisha to review. Posting here so we're aligned before provisioning.

High-level infra plan
- Reserved baseline pool: 2x A100-80GB equivalent (pinned for trial window). This keeps KV caches and model shards resident and gives consistent tail latency.
- Autoscaling: policy owned by Redwood during trial (per Aisha request) — we propose:
  * scale up increments: +2 GPUs per policy trigger (max 8 GPUs)
  * cooldown: 90s
  * minimum scaling duration: 3 minutes (to avoid rapid churn)
  * burst window whitelist: configurable windows (we'll agree on expected hours before trial)
- KV cache: keep warm with periodic synthetic requests; cache warming script included in runbook.
- Preload: model quantization profile we recommend: bf16 + int8 activation path for summary generator to reduce token cost while preserving quality.

Monitoring & observability
- We'll stream per-token latency, tail latencies, KV hit-rate, and per-route cost to the shared Drive & Redwood Console.
- Alerts: cost alert at 70% of agreed budget and hard stop at 110% unless Sparrow toggles override.

Cost sketch (estimates for approval only)
- Baseline (2x A100-80GB equiv): approx $X.XX/hr (redacted here — Marissa will attach formal pricing sheet in the proposal).
- Full burst (8 GPUs) incremental delta: approx 3.5x baseline rate while bursted.

Ownership and runbook
- Provisioning OWNER: Marissa Cole (SE) — will coordinate with Sparrow infra and Redwood ops.
- Runtime support: Dev Patel will be on-call for the first 72 hours of the trial.
- Runbook attached: redwood_trial_runbook.pdf (contains run steps, rollback, smoke tests).

If Aisha approves autoscale policy and approximate cost sketch, we'll schedule provisioning for 2027-05-12 (one week from now).

Marissa Cole
